scope: Post-hoc follow-up on the already selected sequence 3 and inset-excluded sequence 23 frozen spread-memory reads after seeing identical binary masks in the temporal-slot test.
purpose: Measure whether the existing chronological-rank and reversed-slot interventions alter attention features, the raw mask decoder logits, and the native object-presence logits even when the native post-presence binary mask is unchanged. Reuse the frozen captures and interventions; no new trained or untrained weights, new threshold, gating, redetection, label-derived inference input or propagation.
method: Record exactly the existing attention output, the raw SAM mask decoder output before SAM2's existing object-presence mask suppression, the native object-presence logits, and the normal post-suppression output for no-op, rank and permuted temporal slots. The pre-suppression logits are observations only and are never used to produce a substitute prediction or modify the existing presence decision. Save tensor hashes and values to Drive. Maintain equal key counts, original spatial rotary indices, learned checkpoint weights and original query/pointer/condition/insurance data.
verification: First run two fresh seq3 replays and independently recompute the exact substituted positions, attention outputs, raw decoder outputs, presence logits, post-suppression outputs and saved binary masks using a separate process. Verify the normal no-op against the captured original and require no model parameter changes. Then run and independently verify two fresh sequence 23 replays. Report continuous differences and native object-presence scores alongside already audited binary mask scores. No target labels are needed for this diagnostic.
interpretation: A changed internal tensor need not change segmentation; identical binary masks can reflect the checkpoint's existing no-object output behavior. This is a post-hoc same-read diagnostic with no feedback, not evidence that rank slots improve videos, explain generalization, or should be used as an inference policy.
